description: The further obligation the record shows the entity group bears beyond the two commercial-instrument laws: honor the executed SAFE portfolio. Declared as an obligation of the Contracting Office chair in the parked institution genome ('honor the SAFE conversion and liquidity terms on the triggering event'); researched here against the executed instruments and the reconciled portfolio. First-class in the ORG genome because SAFEs bind a legal person, never a statute (org-genome-design.md §0, §4.3 — 'Plus the SAFE obligation').

law.attributes: The 16 executed post-money SAFEs issued by Eir Is Real, Inc. between 2025-03-26 and 2026-02-20 — 13 investors, $215,606.36 total, valuation caps ranging $1M to $12M plus one negotiated $8.5M — every instrument read directly or twice-corroborated, every dollar received matched to paper (portfolio reconciliation closed 2026-07-27). Under the reorganization these transfer to Eir Labs Inc. per the Goodwin-drafted Omnibus SAFE Assignment and Assumption Agreement, whose executed status no located document evidences.
law.aim: Honor the SAFE conversion and liquidity terms of each executed instrument on its triggering event.
law.conditions: Per each instrument's own terms (post-money SAFEs; conversion at the lesser of discount-adjusted price or cap-based price; conversion trigger: next equity financing with gross proceeds ≥ $500,000 excluding SAFE amounts — SAFE Agreements Summary). Carried compliance history, on the record: the June 2025 rescission drafts (stating the original offering 'was not compliant with applicable U.S. securities laws for non-accredited investors') were NEVER signed, so for the re-papered cohort two instruments may technically coexist per person — counsel to determine which instrument governs.
law.or_else: Non-performance on a triggering event is an actionable breach of an executed convertible instrument, enforceable by each holder under the law governing that instrument.
